expectations.text: The reply does not ask about a gap in the research literature, and does not ask what theory, model, or theoretical framework the question tests.
expectations.evidence: The reply never mentions a literature gap or a theory/framework; it only asks: "What would be left for your 700 words to weigh or explain?"

expectations.text: The reply does not name or use a named research-question framework such as PICO, PEO, SPIDER, SPICE, FINER, or PCC.
expectations.evidence: No named framework (PICO, PEO, SPIDER, SPICE, FINER, PCC) appears anywhere in the reply.

expectations.text: The reply raises at most one weakness or missed criterion about the question (it may also say what is good about it).
expectations.evidence: The only weakness raised about the question is that it can be answered yes/no: "Suppose a classmate answered your question with just \"yes.\"" The prompt for a position is about the user's stance, not a flaw in the question.

expectations.text: The reply does not supply a research question for the user: no rewritten, narrowed, broadened, or "improved" version of their question, no example question, and no fill-in-the-blank frame or sentence starter.
expectations.evidence: The reply offers no rewritten or example question and no sentence frame. It asks "Where do you stand right now on your question, in your own words?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Exactly two question marks: "What would be left for your 700 words to weigh or explain?" and "Where do you stand right now on your question, in your own words?"
